description: The project in dirty/ holds the booking service's code, and nothing in it would change a requirement. It returns status 400 where the input asks for 409 and returns no booking ID: both are what the input changes, so they are the feature. Both statements are written from the input and no question is asked because of the code.

must_match.pattern: ^FR-\d+: When an employee books a room for a time slot, the booking service shall store the booking and return the booking ID\.
must_match.why: the complete statement is written from the input's words

must_match.pattern: ^FR-\d+: If [^\n]*overlaps a stored booking of that room, then the booking service shall reject the booking and return HTTP status 409\.
must_match.why: the status the input gives is written, whatever the code returns today
the input names the booking service and the project holds its code, so the skill reads the files

must_not_match.why: a question names the code, which holds no fact that would change a requirement
a status code from the code is in the reply: what the code does differently is the feature
a question asks about what the code does today

manual: Each question is about the input alone: a coverage gap or an open boundary such as time slots that touch.
The transcript shows at most 5 files of booking_service/ read.
